mainTopic: קידושין in front of one witness, and when a single witness or no witness is enough
overview: The amud opens by finishing the מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל on whether witnesses who saw a divorced couple alone together count as witnesses that they lived together. Both agree this does not apply after a divorce from אירוסין. Next, רב (or רבי, in another version) rules that קידושין done in front of one witness has no effect, even if both sides admit it. רב אחדבוי בר אמי challenges this with a ברייתא about two men and a woman arriving from overseas. The גמרא answers that a contradicted single witness is not believed anyway, so the two גיטין are needed only so she can collect her כתובה, following רבי מאיר. רב כהנא and רב פפא then disagree on the final הלכה. רב אשי tests רב כהנא's comparison to money law, and רב כהנא answers that an admission about קידושין affects other people. After that, רב אשי tells two brothers that witnesses exist only for liars, and אביי rules that a single witness is believed when the other person stays silent, supporting this from משניות about חלב and טהרות.

steps.title: Finishing the disagreement on seclusion as proof of intimacy
steps.stepSummary: The end of בית שמאי's view, that seclusion witnesses are not intimacy witnesses, and then בית הלל's opposing view that they are.
steps.simpleTranslation: [בית שמאי hold we do not] say: 'The witnesses of seclusion are the witnesses of intimacy.' And בית הלל hold: we do say that the witnesses of seclusion are the witnesses of intimacy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes a disagreement that began just before this. בית שמאי say witnesses who saw a divorced couple alone together do not count as witnesses that they lived together, and בית הלל say they do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether seeing a man and woman alone together lets us assume intimacy happened. For בית הלל it does, so the intimacy could count as new קידושין and she would need a second גט. For בית שמאי, seclusion alone proves nothing more than seclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses who saw a man and woman alone together
They are the very same (one counts as the other)

phrases.english: [do not] say: these very witnesses of seclusion
phrases.notes: This finishes בית שמאי's line from just before. Their full view is 'we do NOT say' this.

phrases.english: are the very witnesses of intimacy.
And Beit Hillel hold:
We do say: these very witnesses of seclusion
are the very witnesses of intimacy.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל סָבְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a disagreement begun before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית הלל: seclusion witnesses count as intimacy witnesses. בית שמאי: they do not.

steps.title: Both sides agree about a woman divorced from betrothal
steps.stepSummary: Even בית הלל agree that if she was divorced from אירוסין, seclusion is not treated as proof of intimacy.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they certainly agree about a woman divorced from betrothal that we do not say the seclusion witnesses are intimacy witnesses, because he is not familiar with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits בית הלל's rule. If the couple were only engaged (אירוסין) and never lived together, seeing them alone does not make us assume intimacy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל's assumption depends on the couple already being used to each other from living together. A man who only did אירוסין never had that closeness, so we do not assume anything happened when they are alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal, the first stage of marriage before living together
He is not familiar or at ease with her

phrases.english: And they certainly agree about a woman divorced from betrothal

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא אָמְרִינַן הֵן הֵן עֵדֵי יִחוּד
phrases.english: that we do not say: these very witnesses of seclusion
are the very witnesses of intimacy,
because he is not familiar with her.

steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל treat seclusion as proof of intimacy only when the couple had already lived together, not when the divorce came after אירוסין alone.
steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוֹדִים וַדַּאי בְּנִתְגָּרְשָׁה מִן הָאֵירוּסִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits בית הלל's rule from step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After a divorce from אירוסין, seclusion is not assumed to mean intimacy, even according to בית הלל.

steps.title: Betrothal with one witness does not take effect
steps.stepSummary: In the name of רב: קידושין done in front of one witness is ignored, even if both the man and the woman admit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא said in the name of רב: one who betroths with one witness, we do not worry about his betrothal, even if both of them admit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: a new rule that קידושין needs two witnesses to work at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a person's own admission counts for a lot. Here רב says that even when both sides admit the קידושין happened, it means nothing without two witnesses. Step 14 explains why an admission is not enough here.

keyTerms.meaning: We are not concerned; we ignore it

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that two witnesses are needed for קידושין to work, which the rest of the sugya will test.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta said in the name of Rav:
One who betroths with one witness,
we are not concerned about his betrothal,
and even if both of them admit it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic, not tied to the seclusion discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידושין with one witness has no effect, even if both sides admit it.

steps.title: The same rule attributed to the Great Court, meaning רב
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא quotes the same rule from 'the Great Court', and the גמרא explains that this means רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: one who betroths with one witness, the Great Court says we are not concerned about his betrothal. Who is the Great Court? רב.
steps.whatsHappening: A second sage reports the same rule but credits it to 'the Great Court.' The גמרא asks who that is and answers: רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds no new law. It confirms the rule from step 3 and shows that רב was honored with the title 'the Great Court.'

keyTerms.meaning: The Great Court, a title of honor for a leading authority

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
One who betroths with one witness,
the Great Court says:
we are not concerned about his betrothal.
Who is the Great Court? Rav.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the rule of step 3 through another sage
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Great Court, meaning רב, rules that קידושין with one witness has no effect.

steps.title: Another version: the Great Court is רבי
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רבה בר רב הונא quotes רב, who quotes 'the Great Court', and the Great Court is רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רבה בר רב הונא said in the name of רב: one who betroths with one witness, the Great Court says we are not concerned about his betrothal. Who is the Great Court? רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of who said the rule. In this version רב was quoting someone else, and that 'Great Court' was רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling itself does not change. Only the source moves back one generation, from רב to his teacher רבי יהודה הנשיא, which gives the rule even more weight.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב.
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said that Rav said:
One who betroths with one witness,
the Great Court says:
we are not concerned about his betrothal.
Who is the Great Court? Rabbi.

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions give the same law. They only disagree about who first said it.
steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different chain of who said the rule from step 4
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Same rule, with the Great Court identified as רבי.

steps.title: Challenge from the case of two men and a woman from overseas
steps.stepSummary: רב אחדבוי בר אמי quotes a ברייתא: two men each claim the woman as wife and the other as slave, she claims both are her slaves, and she needs two גיטין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחדבוי בר אמי objected: Two men came from overseas with a woman and a bundle. One says: 'She is my wife, he is my slave, this is my bundle.' The other says the same. The woman says: 'These are my two slaves and the bundle is mine.' She needs two גיטין and collects her כתובה from the bundle.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחדבוי begins a challenge against the one-witness rule by quoting a ברייתא. This step sets up the case, and the next step shows why it contradicts רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא rules she needs a גט from each man, so each man's claim of marriage is taken seriously. She also gets her כתובה from the bundle. The question coming next is what kind of evidence each man had.

keyTerms.meaning: The marriage contract payment owed to a wife

phrases.english: Rav Achadvoi bar Ami raised an objection:
Two men who came from overseas,
and a woman with them and a bundle with them.
This one says: This is my wife,
and this one is my slave, and this is my bundle.
And that one says: This is my wife,
and this one is my slave, and this is my bundle.
And the woman says:
These are my two slaves, and the bundle is mine.
She needs two bills of divorce,
and she collects her marriage contract from the bundle.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב אַחָדְבוּי בַּר אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that will be used against the one-witness rule
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that קידושין with one witness has no effect
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires her to get a גט from each man. The next step argues this only makes sense if one-witness קידושין matters.

steps.title: The case must involve only one witness each
steps.stepSummary: If each man had two witnesses, she could not claim they are her slaves. So each must have had one witness, and still she needs a גט, which goes against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If this man has witnesses and that man has witnesses, could she say 'These are my two slaves and the bundle is mine'? Rather, isn't it a case of one witness?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחדבוי finishes his challenge. He proves the ברייתא must be talking about one witness per man, yet it still requires a גט, so one-witness קידושין does matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two full witnesses, the woman's claim that both men are her slaves would be impossible. So the ברייתא must mean each man had only one witness. Since she still needs two גיטין, the ברייתא seems to take one-witness קידושין seriously, against רב's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How do we picture it?
Rather, is it not...? (introduces the only remaining option)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a strong-looking challenge to the one-witness rule. The גמרא will need to answer it.

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If this one has witnesses
and that one has witnesses,
could she say:
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: These are my two slaves and the bundle is mine?
Rather, is it not with one witness!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִי דְּאִית לֵיהּ סָהֲדֵי לְהַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the ברייתא from step 6 goes against רב
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that one-witness קידושין is ignored
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two witnesses for each man is impossible given her claim, so it must be one witness each. Yet she needs two גיטין, so one-witness קידושין counts.

steps.title: A contradicted single witness is not believed anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the challenge. In the ברייתא each man's single witness is contradicted by the other man's witness, and a contradicted single witness is not believed at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really understand it that way? Is a single witness believed when he is contradicted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the reasoning of the challenge from the previous step. It says the ברייתא cannot be teaching that one witness makes קידושין take effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that each man had one witness, and that the need for a גט proves one witness makes קידושין count. But each man's witness is contradicted by the other man's witness, and a lone contradicted witness carries no weight. So the two גיטין must be needed for some other reason.

keyTerms.meaning: And do you really think so? (a phrase that rejects an assumption)
Contradiction, when one testimony is denied by another

phrases.english: And can you really understand it that way?
A single witness who is contradicted
is he believed?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִסְבְּרַאּ? עֵד אֶחָד בְּהַכְחָשָׁה מִי מְהֵימַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference that step 7 built against רב.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The assumption that the ברייתא's need for גיטין comes from believing one witness
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Each witness is contradicted, and a contradicted single witness is not believed at all

steps.title: The two גיטין are only for collecting her כתובה
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees she may marry anyone else. The ברייתא requires two גיטין only so she can collect her כתובה from the bundle, following רבי מאיר, who says movable property is tied to a כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, everyone agrees she is permitted to marry anyone. Here the ברייתא means that she needs two גיטין in order to collect her כתובה from the bundle. This follows רבי מאיר, who says movable property is tied to the payment of a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the ברייתא really means, so it no longer conflicts with רב. The גיטין are about money, not about whether she is married.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As far as איסור goes, she is free to marry anyone, which fits רב. The two גיטין turn each man into a husband who owes her a כתובה, so she can claim payment from the bundle of goods they are fighting over. That only works if movable goods can be collected for a כתובה, which is the view of רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: To permit her to marry anyone
The marriage contract and the money it promises the wife
Are tied to a debt, so the debt can be collected from them

steps.whyThisMatters: With this answer רב's rule survives: one witness does not make קידושין count.

phrases.english: Rather: as for permitting her to marry anyone,
everyone agrees that she is permitted,
and here, this is what it is saying:
She needs two bills of divorce
in order to collect her כתובה from the bundle.
phrases.notes: In the ברייתא's case, the two men were holding a bundle of goods while they argued over her.

phrases.english: And this follows רבי מאיר,
who says movable property is tied to the payment of a כתובה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: לְמִישְׁרֵי לְעָלְמָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דִּשְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new reading of the ברייתא after step 8 knocked out the old one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the ברייתא: the גיטין are needed for money, not for איסור
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two גיטין show that one witness makes קידושין count, which contradicts רב
steps.terutzMaskana: She may marry anyone. The גיטין only let her collect her כתובה from the bundle, following רבי מאיר

steps.title: What is the final ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the final הלכה is about קידושין done in front of one witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was concluded about this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move by asking for the final ruling on קידושין in front of one witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's rule was defended, but the גמרא still wants to know how the הלכה was decided. The answer comes in the next step as a disagreement between אמוראים.

phrases.english: What was concluded about it?
phrases.notes: "It" means קידושין done in front of only one witness.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי הָוֵי עֲלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defending רב to asking for the final halacha.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical ruling on קידושין with one witness

steps.title: רב כהנא and רב פפא disagree
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא says we ignore קידושין done in front of one witness. רב פפא says we must be concerned that they took effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: we are not concerned about his קידושין. רב פפא said: we are concerned about his קידושין.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give opposite answers to the question. רב כהנא agrees with רב, and רב פפא is strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Not concerned" means she is treated as single and needs no גט. "Concerned" means we treat her as possibly married, so she would need a גט before marrying someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: We are not concerned, we ignore it
We are concerned, we take it into account

phrases.english: רב כהנא said:
We are not concerned about his קידושין.
רב פפא said:
We are concerned about his קידושין.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר: אֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין לְקִידּוּשָׁיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10 with a מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב כהנא: one-witness קידושין are ignored. רב פפא: we must be concerned they took effect.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is no single answer. רב כהנא says one-witness קידושין are ignored, and רב פפא says we must be concerned they took effect.

steps.title: רב אשי asks for רב כהנא's source
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי suggests that רב כהנא learns his view from money law through the shared word דבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to רב כהנא: what is your reasoning? Is it that you learn the word "matter" here from the word "matter" in money cases?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי is setting up a challenge. First he spells out what he thinks רב כהנא's source must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה uses the word דבר both for marriage matters and for cases that need two witnesses. Linking the two words (a גזירה שוה) would mean marriage, like money, needs two witnesses. רב אשי will now test where that comparison leads.

keyTerms.meaning: A גזירה שוה built on the word "matter" appearing in two places

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב כָּהֲנָא
phrases.english: רב אשי said to רב כהנא:
What is your reasoning?
That you learn "matter" and "matter" from money cases?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב כָּהֲנָא: מַאי דַּעְתָּיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the source behind רב כהנא's view in step 11, to prepare a challenge.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב כהנא's source is the גזירה שוה of דבר דבר from money law

steps.title: Then an admission should count like a hundred witnesses
steps.stepSummary: If marriage is compared to money, then an admission should also count, as it does in money cases. Here both the man and the woman admit to the קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as there the admission of a litigant is like a hundred witnesses, so too here the admission of a litigant should be like a hundred witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי challenges רב כהנא. If you compare marriage to money, you must take the whole comparison, including the power of an admission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In money law a person's own admission obligates him completely. If marriage follows money law, the admission of the man and the woman should make the קידושין count. That goes against רב כהנא's view that we ignore them even when both admit.

phrases.english: If so, just as there
the admission of a litigant
is like a hundred witnesses,
so too here, the admission of a litigant
should be like a hundred witnesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה לְהַלָּן הוֹדָאַת בַּעַל דִּין כְּמֵאָה עֵדִים דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the source named in step 12 to attack רב כהנא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's ruling that we ignore one-witness קידושין even when both sides admit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If marriage is learned from money law, then the money-law rule that an admission is like a hundred witnesses should apply too

steps.title: An admission about קידושין affects other people
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that an admission about money hurts only the person admitting, while an admission about קידושין affects others too, so it does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: there, he does not make others liable. Here, he makes others liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא defends himself. He explains why an admission works for money but not for קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person may obligate himself, and that is why a money admission works. Admitting to קידושין creates איסורים that reach beyond the two people, and a person cannot admit something that obligates others. So the comparison to money does not carry over this rule.
steps.whatToRemember: רב כהנא holds that one-witness קידושין are ignored even if both admit. Marriage is compared to money, which needs two witnesses. But an admission does not work here, because it affects other people and not just the one admitting.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רב כהנא is answering רב אשי.

phrases.english: There, he does not make others liable;
here, he makes others liable.
phrases.notes: Admitting to קידושין affects other people too, like whom these two are allowed to marry.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם לָא קָא חָיֵיב לְאַחֲרִינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge from step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the two cases: self-obligation versus affecting others
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison to money should make an admission of קידושין count like a hundred witnesses
steps.terutzMaskana: An admission only works when it obligates the person admitting, and an admission of קידושין affects others

steps.title: Two brothers ask whether a property split needs witnesses
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא and רב אדא סבא divided their shared property between themselves and asked רב אשי whether the split is valid without witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא and רב אדא סבא, the sons of רב מרי בר איסור, divided their property between them. They came to רב אשי and asked: The תורה says 'by the mouth of two witnesses.' Is that only so people cannot back out later? We are not backing out. Or maybe a matter only takes effect with witnesses?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story. Two brothers split their property without witnesses and ask רב אשי whether that split counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The brothers give two options. Maybe witnesses are just protection against someone backing out later; since neither of them is backing out, they would not need witnesses. Or maybe witnesses are what make the deal take effect at all, so without them nothing happened.

keyTerms.meaning: 'by the mouth of two witnesses', the פסוק that requires two witnesses
to back out, to go back on a deal

steps.whyThisMatters: This question ties into the larger discussion. If witnesses are only needed against denial, then an act everyone admits to might stand even without proper witnesses.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra and Rav Adda the Elder,
the sons of Rav Mari bar Issur,
divided their property with each other.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתוֹ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי, אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: They came before Rav Ashi and said to him:
The Merciful One said, "By the mouth of two witnesses",
so that if they want to back out,
they cannot back out of it.
And we are not backing out.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא לָא מִקַּיְימָא מִלְּתָא אֶלָּא בְּסָהֲדֵי?
phrases.english: Or perhaps a matter only takes effect with witnesses?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתוֹ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי, אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the talk about admission and קידושין, the גמרא turns to a related question about the role of witnesses.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are witnesses needed only to stop someone from denying a deal, or are they needed for the deal to take effect at all?

steps.title: Witnesses are only needed for liars
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that witnesses exist only in case someone lies; if nobody denies the deal, it stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Witnesses were created only for liars.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the brothers. Witnesses are only there in case someone lies, so their property split is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי picks the first option. Witnesses do not create the deal; they only protect it against someone who might deny it. When both sides agree it happened, nothing more is needed.
steps.whatToRemember: In money matters, witnesses are needed only against denial. If both sides agree, the deal stands without them.

phrases.english: He said to them:
Witnesses were not created
except for liars.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא אִיבְּרוֹ סָהֲדֵי אֶלָּא לְשַׁקָּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the brothers' question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Witnesses are only protection against liars. A deal both sides admit to is valid without them.

steps.title: One witness about eating חלב is believed if the person stays silent
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that if one witness tells someone he ate חלב and the person says nothing, the witness is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: If one witness tells someone, 'You ate חלב,' and that person stays silent, the witness is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a new rule. One witness is believed about a sin if the accused person does not deny it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually one witness is not enough. Here the person's silence works like agreeing, so the single witness is accepted. This continues the idea that when nobody denies something, full witnesses are not needed.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
If one witness said to him, "You ate forbidden fat,"
and that person stays silent, the witness is believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אָמַר לוֹ עֵד אֶחָד ״אָכַלְתָּ חֵלֶב״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement that fits the same theme: when nobody denies something, less proof is needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One witness who says a person ate חלב is believed if that person stays silent.

steps.title: A משנה supports אביי about חלב
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says the person is exempt when he denies it. That implies that if he stays silent, the witness is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא also taught: If one witness says 'You ate חלב' and the person says 'I did not eat,' he is exempt. The reason is that he said 'no.' But if he stayed silent, the witness would be believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to back up אביי. It reads the משנה carefully to draw the same rule out of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says the person is exempt when he actively denies the witness. The גמרא reasons that this is the only reason he is exempt. So if he had stayed silent, the witness would be believed, just as אביי said.

keyTerms.meaning: and our תנא also taught this

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה never says 'if he is silent, the witness is believed.' The גמרא is inferring that from the fact that the משנה only exempts someone who says 'no.'

phrases.english: And our tanna also taught:
If one witness said to him, "You ate forbidden fat,"
and that person says, "I did not eat it," he is exempt.
The reason is that he said "no";
but if he was silent, the witness is believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא תּוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support from a משנה for אביי's rule in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's rule that one witness about חלב is believed when the person stays silent.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה that exempts the person only when he says 'I did not eat.' The גמרא infers that silence means the witness is believed.

steps.title: One witness about impure טהרות is believed if the owner stays silent
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives the same rule for טהרות: one witness who says they became impure is believed if the owner says nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי said: If one witness tells someone, 'Your טהרות became impure,' and that person stays silent, the witness is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second rule that matches the first one. This time it is about pure food becoming impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case changes from a sin (eating חלב) to the purity of food. The logic stays the same: when the owner does not deny it, the single witness is accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: your טהרות: food kept in a state of purity

phrases.english: And Abaye said:
If one witness said to him, "Your pure items became impure,"
and that person stays silent, the witness is believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אָמַר לוֹ עֵד אֶחָד ״נִטְמְאוּ טׇהֳרוֹתֶיךָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel second statement by אביי, built the same way as step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One witness who says someone's טהרות became impure is believed if the owner stays silent.

steps.title: A משנה supports אביי about impure טהרות
steps.stepSummary: A משנה exempts the owner only when he denies the impurity. That implies that if he stays silent, the witness is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא also taught: If one witness says 'They became impure' and the owner says 'They did not become impure,' he is exempt. The reason is that he said 'no.' But if he stayed silent, the witness would be believed.
steps.whatsHappening: Just like before, the גמרא brings a משנה that supports אביי's second rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works exactly like step 18. The owner is exempt only because he denied the witness, so silence would mean the witness is believed. Both of אביי's rules end up resting on the same kind of reading of a משנה.
steps.whatToRemember: In all of these cases, silence counts like agreeing. When nobody denies something, a single witness, or even no witnesses in money matters, can be enough.

phrases.english: And our tanna also taught:
If one witness says, "They became impure,"
and that person says, "They did not become impure," he is exempt.
The reason is that he said "no";
but if he was silent, the witness is believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא תּוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support from a משנה for אביי's rule in step 19, the same way step 18 did.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's rule that one witness about impure טהרות is believed when the owner stays silent.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה that exempts the owner only when he says 'they did not become impure.' The גמרא infers that silence means the witness is believed.

steps.title: אביי opens another ruling about one witness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces another statement of אביי that starts with one witness saying something to a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי also said: if one witness says to someone...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new ruling from אביי, again about a single witness speaking to someone. Only the opening words appear here; the actual case and ruling come in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'and' (וְ) shows this is another ruling from the same speaker, אביי, added to the ones about חלב and טהרות. The opening 'one witness says to him' matches those earlier rulings. That suggests the same question is coming up again: is a lone witness believed when the other person does not deny it?

keyTerms.meaning: A single witness. Normally two witnesses are needed to establish a fact in court.

phrases.english: And אביי said:
If one witness says to him:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another ruling of אביי that opens like his rulings in Steps 17 and 19, which were each supported from a משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the opening appears here: a case in which a single witness tells someone something. The case itself and the ruling come next.
